messages:
Maya D: paging everyone — Saxony Health (enterprise account) is reporting 500s on dedicated routing since ~08:04 UTC. I’m seeing error spike in prod-router logs. IncidentBot: incident created INC-20240710-53, severity: P1. Pager sent to oncall.
Jonas P: oncall here, grabbing. can someone paste the most recent alerts/hosts affected? I only see a few 503s on edge-3.
Maya D: looks like traffic to dedicated pool 'ded-saxony-1' is failing health checks. LB returns 502 -> backend reports KV cache errors. Logs:
```
[08:03:58] backend/ded-saxony-1: kvcache: eviction-failure: unable to allocate slab; err=OOM
[08:04:01] router/proxy: upstream returned 502 for req id=ab12cd
```
Jonas P: ok noted. Ashwin — you were on the last deploy for ded-saxony-1? any config changes?
Ashwin R: I rolled a minor kernel param tweak yesterday (net.core.somaxconn) but nothing touching caching. I’ll SSH into the instance now, sending command:
```
ssh redwood@ded-saxony-1-03
sudo systemctl status inference-runtime
```
IncidentBot: @oncall acknowledged INC-20240710-53. Next update expected in 15m.
Karen S: triage note for comms: Saxony Health is on a Reserved Dedicated contract with enterprise support. They have high-touch contacts: primary ops (ops@saxony.health), escalation (sec-ops@saxony.health), and mobile oncall +1-555-0133. They expect an update within 30 minutes.
Elena V: drafting customer-facing impact statement below — please edit for tone/accuracy.
Elena V: (draft)
"We are currently experiencing a degraded service affecting Saxony Health’s dedicated routing (ded-saxony-1). Some requests are returning 5xx errors; this may impact patient lookup and triage workflows. Our engineering team is actively investigating and applying mitigations. We will provide updates every 30 minutes and when service is restored. We apologize for the disruption and will send a follow-up with root cause and remediation steps." 
Maya D: good start. Add: "No data exfiltration detected; patient data remains encrypted at rest and in transit." then approve.
Elena V: updated.
Jonas P: operational notes for internal responders: do not restart the entire node unless asked by infra lead — restarting can trigger cache warm-up storms and affect other tenants. Instead, disable routing to the failing pod and failover to ded-saxony-2.
Maya D: I’m running the failover now:
```
redwood-cli routing set-weight --pool ded-saxony-1 --weight 0 --until 1718007521
redwood-cli routing set-weight --pool ded-saxony-2 --weight 1
```
Support-Bot: Route change applied by maya_d at 08:10 UTC. Traffic now shifting to ded-saxony-2.
Ashwin R: confirming: ded-saxony-2 is up and healthy. No KV errors there. Error rate dropped from 18% to 0.9% in 2 minutes.
Jonas P: good. continuing investigation: initial hypothesis is localized memory pressure (OOM) on ded-saxony-1 due to cache config regression. I’ll open a short-lived maintenance ticket for infra to inspect kernel params and cgroup limits.
Maya D: comms check — status page update to post? Suggested copy:
"We are investigating increased 5xx errors impacting Saxony Health’s dedicated routing. Mitigation (traffic failover) is in progress. Customers on this pool may experience intermittent failures. Next update: in 30 minutes or upon resolution."
Elena V: also preparing targeted email to Saxony ops list. Draft below — keep it concise and actionable:
"Saxony Health team,
We’re actively mitigating an incident affecting your dedicated routing (ded-saxony-1). Impact: intermittent 5xx errors affecting patient lookup and some batch jobs. Mitigation: We have shifted traffic to a healthy standby pool (ded-saxony-2) to reduce errors. Action required: none at this time. Expected next update: in 30 minutes. Contact: ops@saxony.health, emergency: +1-555-0133. — Redwood Inference Support"
Karen S: add a note about rollback window and whether any queued requests need retrying: "Clients should retry idempotent requests; non-idempotent workflows may need manual reconciliation." 
Elena V: added that line.
IncidentBot: update scheduled: 08:40 UTC.
Jonas P: internal ops checklist going forward:
- keep routing weight at 0 for ded-saxony-1 until infra confirms memory config (ashwin + infra)
- collect heap dumps from failing host (if safe)
- check autoscaler for cache warm-up behavior
- prepare rollback of yesterday’s kernel tweak if root cause points to it
Ashwin R: starting diagnostic snapshot now. Commands:
```
sudo journalctl -u inference-runtime -n 500 > /tmp/ir-log-sax1.log
sudo /opt/redwood/tools/cache-inspect --dump > /tmp/cache-dump-sax1.json
```
Maya D: who’s owning the customer message send? I can do the email and page the Saxony ops mobile number.
Karen S: Maya, you send the email (use the draft), and cc me + Elena. Also call the escalation number once the email is sent.
Maya D: sending email now. Email sent at 08:15 UTC. Placing call to +1-555-0133.
Support-Bot: email(s) to ops@saxony.health delivered. Call status: voicemail left.
Elena V: status page updated (public) with the suggested copy and marked as "partial outage — routing". Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20240710-53
Jonas P: infra ping — @ashwin, @infra-lead — can you confirm cgroup/memory limits on ded-saxony-1 and whether the kernel param change could increase memory overhead?
Ashwin R: infra-lead responded in PM: the somaxconn tweak is network accept queue only; not expected to affect memory. However, one of the runtime sidecars got a config bump to cache.max_entries=5M yesterday (rolled as part of a batch). That may explain extra memory pressure.
Jonas P: that aligns. If cache.max_entries increased, memory footprint rose. Plan: reduce cache.max_entries on ded-saxony-1 and restart the affected sidecar in place (no full host restart). Ashwin — can you patch and restart the sidecar live?
Ashwin R: applying config change now and restarting sidecar with graceful restart:
```
kubectl set env deployment/saxony-sidecar CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=2000000 -n enterprise-saxony
kubectl rollout restart deployment/saxony-sidecar -n enterprise-saxony --timeout=120s
```
IncidentBot: maintenance window created for node ded-saxony-1 at 08:20 UTC.
Maya D: update for the customer: errors are down 98% after failover, and we've scheduled a targeted maintenance on the affected pool to permanently fix config. Sending follow-up update to ops@saxony.health.
Elena V: follow-up draft:
"Update: We have shifted traffic to a healthy standby pool and applied a targeted configuration change to reduce memory pressure on the affected host. Error rates have dropped significantly. We will monitor for 1 hour and provide a final report outlining root cause and remediation. No action needed on your side at this time."
Jonas P: handing off to night oncall in 35 minutes. @Elena, @Karen — please review the post-incident template for the RCA. We need to include the specific internal change (cache.max_entries regression), timeline, remediation (reduce entries + add preflight mem checks), and customer impact statement.
Karen S: I’ll prepare the customer-tailored RCA follow-up. Include list of impacted account IDs and contact routing summary. A sample impacted account list:
- Saxony Health, tenant_id: ten-9921, contact: ops@saxony.health, escalation: sec-ops@saxony.health
- MinorLab (shared routing fallback), tenant_id: ten-9932, contact: eng@minorlab.ai
Maya D: note that MinorLab saw brief increased latency during the failover window (08:10–08:12) but no errors — include that in cross-tenant impact.
IncidentBot: final update posted to thread at 08:28 UTC: mitigation successful, monitoring.
Elena V: lodging final customer follow-up now that we have the arc of mitigation. Draft RCA header:
"Root cause: regression in cache configuration (cache.max_entries increased during config batch), which led to memory exhaustion on a dedicated host causing service 5xx. Remediation: reduce cache entries, add memory guardrails, add pre-deploy mem-check in CI, and implement automatic failover tests for dedicated pools."
Jonas P: will open RFC for guardrails and preflight checks tomorrow. Handing over to night oncall @Elena for monitoring. I’ll stay available for escalation until 09:00 UTC.
Elena V: taking over monitoring. I have the runbook and will post final customer RCA once infra validates the patch. Thanks team.
Maya D: thanks all. Closing the active pager. :thumbsup:
